tool_args.new_string: Per-step oracle labeling assigns routing labels by comparing single-step outcomes under each computation modality. Under sparse terminal rewards, this approach degenerates: on ScienceWorld \cite{scienceworld-2022}, 97.4\% of steps produce identical intermediate scores regardless of modality (5{,}726 of 5{,}878 steps across 11 prescreened task types), yielding no per-step routing signal. The 97.4\% tie rate arises because ScienceWorld assigns rewards only at episode termination; intermediate steps update environment state but do not change the score, so a per-step oracle can only distinguish strategies through downstream consequences visible at episode end. Episode-level comparison is therefore the principled granularity for sparse-reward environments, not a fallback from per-step analysis: it directly measures whether one strategy produces better terminal outcomes than the other, bypassing the uninformative intermediate steps entirely.
